correctness.rationale: For every finite field, arbitrary sandwich rank, arbitrary positive tuple arity, and all valid core signatures, direct block multiplication gives B_i^2=B_i, B_i C_i=C_i, D_i B_i=D_i, E_i=D_i C_i. The pairwise equations force one shared C and D per nonzero signature, giving exactly q to the power (m+n-2r)D lifts. Explicit invertible L,R with RAL=A simultaneously untwist all idempotents; diagonalizing commuting projections yields unrestricted commutant blocks M_d for each nonzero signature and one (m-D)x(n-D) residual rectangle. The block product is an algebra isomorphism preserving ordinary matrix ranks, giving the full rank polynomial. Every signature count and full rank polynomial was compared with direct original-multiplication enumeration in ten cases including q=2,3, tuple length 3, rank-zero A, and rectangular shapes. The finite checker is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full ordinary-rank centralizer spectrum is an intrinsic natural invariant of a family of nonunital finite matrix semigroups central to Munn rings. This unbounded all-arity classification of **unrestricted** common-commutant matrices goes substantially beyond a single projection or a pairwise idempotent count: its rank-polynomial block factorization is independent of the sandwich rank at fixed joint signature, while pairs with identical marginal idempotent ranks can have centralizers of sizes 32 or 8. The exact mixed polynomial provides a reusable object for investigating common commutants, not an arbitrary narrow slice or numerical example. Standard spectral counts are credited; the contribution is their nontrivial interaction with the arbitrary final matrix and rectangular sandwich product.
